content:
Bruno Silva: heads up: i'm putting up terraform changes for Private upgrades.
- PR 1332: version pinning + upgrade window vars
- PR 1340: artifact mirror endpoints (for on-prem + VPC customers w/ internal registries)

main question: how hard do we want to push backwards compatibility here? i can make everything optional w/ defaults to current behavior, but there's some sharp edges (e.g. if mirror is set, we need to re-point chart repo + image registry).

Irene Choi: can you drop links? also, please please no breaking change on existing module consumers. we have a handful of customers pinned to older module versions and they expect `terraform apply` to be no-op unless they opt in.

Bruno Silva: yep
- https://github.com/redwood/redwood-terraform/pull/1332
- https://github.com/redwood/redwood-terraform/pull/1340

proposal in 1332:
- `private_release_version` (string, optional) -> if unset, keep existing "latest compatible" resolution
- `upgrade_window` (object-ish via strings, bc no nested) -> `upgrade_window_start`, `upgrade_window_end`, `upgrade_window_tz`
- `require_explicit_version` (bool default false) -> future gate?

proposal in 1340:
- `artifact_mirror_chart_repo_url` (optional)
- `artifact_mirror_container_registry` (optional)
- `artifact_mirror_blob_base_url` (optional for installer bundle downloads)

Devon Price: +1 on opt-in only. also consider we can't do real object types if you're avoiding nested, but terraform itself can. do we actually have a constraint there? (for the docs we might, but tf vars can be objects)

Bruno Silva: sorry, to clarify: terraform vars are normal types. i meant *we* have customers who pass via env var strings / TF Cloud workspace vars, so keeping it string-friendly.

Connor O'Brien: re: version pinning, we need to be explicit about which "version" that is:
- installer version
- platform control plane version
- helm chart version

right now customers assume module version ~= platform version, which isn't always true.
can we name it `private_platform_version` and have module translate to installer/chart versions internally?

Bruno Silva: yeah that's in the PR discussion. i currently have:
- `private_platform_version` (e.g. "1.18.3")
- module maps to `installer_version` + `chart_version` via a lookup table we ship in the module

but that lookup table is where backwards compat questions come in (keeping it updated + what happens when version not in table).

Quentin Harris: mapping table needs to match the compatibility policy in main repo (the one i'm maintaining). if tf module has its own matrix that drifts, we'll get weird "tf lets you" but installer blocks you.

suggestion: module should NOT guess. it should accept explicit chart + installer versions, OR call out to a small "release manifest" artifact that we publish per platform release.

Irene Choi: +1 release manifest. fewer places to update.

Fatima Noor: for on-prem/air-gapped: mirror endpoints are never just a single URL.
- some customers have chart repo in Artifactory
- images in Harbor
- blob artifacts on an internal nginx
- plus custom CA chain

do we have a place to pass `custom_ca_bundle` or `additional_trust_anchors` to the installer? otherwise mirror URLs won't work in practice.

Victor Alvarez: networking angle: if we add mirror endpoints, we need to be clear on TLS + DNS expectations.
- do we support `http://` at all? (some on-prem are stuck)
- if we allow it, it should be a warning + explicit `allow_insecure_mirror = true`

also for VPC customers, mirror might be reachable only via private DNS. prechecks should validate reachability, but terraform can at least validate it's a sane URL.

Bruno Silva: good call. in 1340 i added validation for scheme in `chart_repo_url` / `blob_base_url`, but it's currently permissive.

what do we want as default?
- require https unless `allow_insecure_artifact_mirror = true`

Vanessa Ortiz: default should be secure. but we need an escape hatch for design partners, otherwise we'll block beta. make it loud.

Connor O'Brien: for backwards compatibility: making new vars optional is necessary but not sufficient.
there's also the behavior of "no version pin" today.

if you keep resolving "latest" by default, upgrades can happen accidentally when someone runs apply.
for Private, that's pretty scary.

can we at least add a warning output like:
"WARNING: private_platform_version not set; module will track release channel X"

Bruno Silva: yep. i can add an output `upgrade_risk_notice` that prints when version is unset.
terraform can't really warn, but we can:
- emit output
- and add a `null_resource` w/ `triggers` + `local-exec` echo (gross)

Irene Choi: please don't do local-exec warnings :grimacing:
outputs are fine + docs.

redwood-ci-bot: PR 1340 - check "terraform fmt" failed on 2 files. (run `terraform fmt -recursive`)

Bruno Silva: ack will fix.

Fatima Noor: on the CA bundle: installer supports `--ca-bundle-path` in the on-prem flow (at least in the draft). can terraform pass that through to the helm chart values / installer config?

Bruno Silva: today module renders an installer config yaml (via template) and passes it to a kubernetes job.
so we can add
- `artifact_mirror_ca_bundle_pem` (sensitive)
- write to a k8s secret
- mount to installer job

but i want sign-off from security before we encourage CA PEM in TF state.

Irene Choi: yeah, careful: anything in TF vars ends up in state (even if sensitive, it's still stored). we should avoid telling customers to put private cert material in terraform unless we have a clear story.

Victor Alvarez: alternative: have customers pre-create secret out-of-band (kubectl / external secrets) and terraform just references it by name.
like `artifact_mirror_ca_secret_name`.

Bruno Silva: that's better. i'll add:
- `artifact_mirror_ca_secret_name` optional
- if set, we mount it
- if not, no extra trust anchors

Devon Price: +1. same pattern for registry creds (reference existing secret). don't reinvent.

Connor O'Brien: also pls ensure we don't change existing secret names/labels. upgrade path should keep them stable.

Bruno Silva: noted. i'll keep existing `redwood-private-registry` secret logic untouched unless mirror vars are set.

Quentin Harris: on the "release manifest" thing: we can publish something like:
`https://artifacts.redwood.ai/private/releases/1.18.3/manifest.json`
with chart version, installer version, and sha256s.

then terraform can fetch it via `data "http"` if allowed, or via mirror base url in on-prem.

Irene Choi: that lines up w/ the on-prem bundle manifest doc too. nice.

Fatima Noor: for air-gapped, we can't `data http` to public internet.
but if they set `artifact_mirror_blob_base_url`, module can fetch manifest from there (or we require they check it in locally).

Bruno Silva: ok, plan:
1) keep `private_platform_version` optional (no breaking)
2) if set: resolve via release manifest (public by default, mirror if provided)
3) if unset: maintain current behavior (channel tracking), but add explicit output saying it's not pinned

open question: do we need to support older module versions reading the new vars? (no)

action items:
- [Bruno] update PR 1340 to require https unless `allow_insecure_artifact_mirror = true`
- [Bruno] add `artifact_mirror_ca_secret_name` (not PEM) + docs
- [Connor] confirm naming for platform vs installer vs chart version in release train notes
- [Quentin] confirm manifest schema/fields we can rely on

Connor O'Brien: works. ping me once you push the changes; i'll review for release-train alignment.

Irene Choi: please tag @Marcus Lin / @Hanae Suzuki when you add secret handling, even if it's "reference existing secret". security will want to sanity check.

Bruno Silva: will do. thanks all.

Victor Alvarez: one more: if mirror endpoints are set, make sure module doesn't assume port 443 only. some customers have `https://registry.local:5443` etc.

Bruno Silva: yep, URL parser keeps port. i'll add a test case.

Vanessa Ortiz: :thumbsup: and for beta, can we add an example tfvars snippet in the PR description? support will ask.

Bruno Silva: yup, adding.

redwood-ci-bot: PR 1340 - all checks passed.
